interpretation: This is a hard synthetic math benchmark, not market evidence.
GBM and Heston are different models; their outputs should not be expected to match.
Fair coupon is challenger output and is not production-approved.

canonical_phoenix_engine.reason: current canonical engine uses simplified coupon/autocall semantics and does not consume full structured-note schedule; do not treat its output as the same hard problem solution

review.interpretation: The benchmark is synthetic and not directly comparable to the canonical Phoenix engine due to simplified coupon/autocall semantics. The public GBM challenger PVs converge to ~117.38 with SE ~0.1140 at 32k paths, while the Heston model yields a lower PV of 114.7748 with SE 0.3468. The path-level reference payoff of 68.0 suggests significant discrepancies in pricing mechanics.
objections: Lack of direct comparability to the canonical Phoenix engine due to simplified semantics.
Synthetic nature of the benchmark with no market or OOS claims.
Discrepancies between GBM and Heston models (PV difference of ~2.61).
Path-level reference payoff (68.0) deviates significantly from model PVs (~117).
acceptance_tests: Verify convergence of GBM challenger PVs across increasing path counts (1k, 2k, 4k, 8k, 16k, 32k).
Compare Heston model PVs with GBM challenger PVs under identical parameters.
Validate path-level payoff logic against model PVs.
Test coupon/autocall semantics in the canonical Phoenix engine against the benchmark.
review.next_experiment: Implement a refined Phoenix engine with explicit coupon/autocall semantics and compare against the synthetic benchmark using the same path-level payoff logic.
